I derived the configuration myself and found that none of the three answers matches my result. I chose the nearest one.

**Setup.** Take the origin at the ellipse's center. Since F₁W = F₂W = 45, W is an endpoint of the minor axis. So CD is parallel to the major axis, and Z on FA is the opposite minor-axis endpoint. This gives a = 45.

The rectangle's side AC equals the distance between lines CD and FA, which is 2b. Congruence with △ABC gives F₁F₂ = AC, so 2c = 2b and b = c. Then a² = 2b², so b² = 2025/2.

Triangle ABC has AB = BC = 45 and AC = 45√2, so the angle at B is 90°.

**Coordinates.** Put the major axis on the x-axis, CD on y = −b and FA on y = b. Then:
- B lies on the x-axis, and line BA has slope 1.
- Tangency of BA to the ellipse gives a² + b² = (p + b)², so p + b = √3·b.
- By symmetry, line EF has slope −1 and y-intercept √3·b.
- The tangent point on EF is Y = (2b/√3, b/√3).
- Z = (0, b) and F₁ = (−b, 0).

**Point Q.** Q = (q, −b) lies on CD, and ZQ ⊥ F₁Y gives q = 2b(2 − √3).

**Area.** The diagonals F₁Y and ZQ are perpendicular, so the area is ½·|F₁Y|·|ZQ|.
- |F₁Y|² = b²(8/3 + 4/√3)
- |ZQ|² = b²(32 − 16√3)
- Their product is b⁴·(64/3), so |F₁Y|·|ZQ| = b²·8/√3.

The area is 4b²/√3 = 4050/√3 = 1350√3 ≈ 2338.

**Comparison.** The candidate answers are 2025, 1012.5 and 225, and none equals 1350√3. All three solutions assert their key lengths without derivation. Solution 1 (2025) is numerically closest to my value, so I pick it, but it is not correct by my calculation.

CHOICE: 1
